gloss: to call (elections, a strike); to announce (a competition, tender); to advertise (posts); to proclaim
why: Main current senses (call elections, announce a competition/posts) first; "proclaim" is κηρύσσω.

gloss: thanksgiving service (Te Deum, e.g. on national holidays); doxology
why: In today's Greek the word mostly names the thanksgiving service; put it first.
"οι Γραικοί κατά τους Λατίνους" is an invented phrase.
"απώτατος στόχος" is unusual (απώτερος στόχος is the set phrase); προσεχής/άμεσος are not true opposites; απέχω is not the same root.
ευρωπαϊστής is a noun, not a near-synonym.
αποικία (colony) is not a near-synonym in the main sense.
δημοφιλής means popular, not widespread.
περιθάλπω means to look after/nurse, not to house.
The set phrase is "συνδετικός κρίκος", not "συνεκτικός κρίκος".
αβασίλευτος mainly means "never-setting" and is not a clear opposite.
The English was wrong: it is a parliamentary republic with a president, not a presidential republic.
"οριοθετώ τα όρια μου" says the same thing twice and is missing an accent (όριά).
"ο συνωστισμός της Σμύρνης" refers to a disputed textbook phrase and is not a collocation; αραίωση is not a true opposite.

gloss: clientelist, patronage (πελατειακό κράτος: patronage state); client (attrib., e.g. πελατειακή βάση)
why: Clientelist sense (πελατειακό κράτος) is the one met most in news; put it first.
σηκώνομαι (get up) is not a near-synonym of rising from the dead.
The natural order is "ασφυκτικά γεμάτος"; "ασφυκτικά πλαίσια" is uncommon.
"βιωτός κόσμος" is invented.
ελαστικός is not an opposite of tyrannical.
αποπροσανατολίζω (disorient) is not a near-synonym of divert.

gloss: cash (attrib.); treasury; financial (also spelled ταμειακός, the more common form)
why: The more common standard spelling is ταμειακός (from ταμείο, e.g. ταμειακή μηχανή).
μιμητής is not a true opposite.
μακρόχρονος means lasting years, not hours.

gloss: indicative; illustrative, telling (είναι ενδεικτικό ότι); (as noun, το ενδεικτικό) school report
why: Fixed the "n. noun" typo and added the common "telling" sense (είναι ενδεικτικό ότι).

gloss: to let off steam; to unwind; (of tension, a crisis) to be defused, ease
why: Added the frequent news sense (tension or a crisis is defused) that the collocation already uses.
μονόδρομος is a noun (one-way street), not an adjective opposite.
"η ήσσων αντίσταση" is not a natural phrase (the idiom is "η γραμμή της ελάχιστης αντίστασης").
αδιάφορος means indifferent, not uninvolved.
ορμόνη is not the same root.
"καθαυτό πρόβλημα" before the noun is doubtful.
χωριάτισσα is not a true opposite.

example.en: Don't pour disinfectants down the sink.

why: Everyday sense is germicide/disinfectant; "biocide" is technical. The example's English now matches.
"τονικό ποτό" is not natural (τονωτικό ποτό, τόνικ).
δημοτική (Demotic, the standard language) is not a near-synonym of everyday speech.
"ιδίωμα του χαρακτήρα" is not a natural collocation.
ονομάζω/αποκαλώ fit only the minor "name" sense, not baptise.
ψευδοδιανοούμενος (pseudo-intellectual) is not a near-synonym.
"wilful" is negative in English; θεληματικός (of chin, character) means strong-willed/determined. "θεληματική προσφορά" is unusual (εθελοντική).
καθηγητής (secondary/university teacher) is not a near-synonym.
ακραίος (extremist) is not a near-synonym.

gloss: (secondary-school) teacher of Greek language and literature; philologist
why: Learners meet the secondary-school teacher sense most often; put it first.
αιτιατική is another case, not an opposite.
"κατορθώνω τον στόχο μου" is unidiomatic (πετυχαίνω τον στόχο μου).
"ηθικό φρόνημα" does not mean morale (that is ηθικό).
"με κάθε λογισμό" is invented.
A made bed is "στρωμένο κρεβάτι", not "στρωτό".

gloss: (learned, archaic) fish (in science and church symbolism; everyday word ψάρι); (pl. Ιχθύες) Pisces (star sign)

collocations.el: ο ιχθύς εκ της κεφαλής όζει
collocations.en: the fish rots from the head (proverb)

why: The collocations were invented; replaced them with the known proverb and the zodiac sign, and added the Pisces sense.
"ακτοπλοΐα και ναυτιλία" is not a set phrase and the English was wrong; ναυσιπλοΐα means navigation, not shipping.

gloss: aromatic herb (e.g. parsley, dill); spice; (pl.) perfumes, aromatics
why: The main sense today is aromatic herbs (parsley, dill and the like); put it first.
"ρήτορας της Βουλής" is not a set phrase.
μέτριος (mediocre) is not a near-synonym.
